item.title: François Kevorkian, Dimitri From Paris - The Nassau Excursion
item.description: Label: Rush Hour | Prix: 16,00 € | Style: Boogie , House, Dub
item.content:encoded:
Label: Rush Hour

Prix: 16,00 €

Style: Boogie , House, Dub

House MasterpieceSome 30 years after they first met in the DJ booth of Tokyo’s Spacelab Yellow nightclub, close friends François Kevorkian and Dimitri From Paris have finally joined forces in the studio. The result is The Nassau Excursion, a dazzlingly good three-track EP inspired by their joint love of disco and boogie-era dance records made at Island Records’ Compass Point Studio in the Bahamas. Across three essential tracks, François and Dimitri explore and celebrate this distinctive Caribbean post-disco sound – one where weighty basslines and heavy drum machine beats rub shoulders with early ‘80s synths, dub-style production, heady hand percussion patterns and arrangements drenched in space echo and tape delay.[info sheet from distr.]

Tracklist:

  • A. The Compass Point
  • B1. 2 Da Riddim
  • B2. Steppers Revenge

item.title: Demuja - Title Txt
item.description: Label: Peach Discs | Prix: 16,00 € | Style: House , Dub House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Peach Discs

Prix: 16,00 €

Style: House , Dub House

Exiled Bristolians (well, former Bristol dwellers at least) Shanti Celeste and Gramarcy welcome Saltzburg sort Demuja aka long-serving producer Bernhardt Weiss to Peach Discs for the very first time. He hits the ground running on opener 'Stop Asking Me', a bouncy analogue house number marked out by tech-tinged synth motifs and a sturdy deep house groove, before reaching for tribal house style beats on the dark, weighty, forthright and organ-splashed hypnotism of 'Oldhead'. 'Say No More' is a warmer and more rhythmically fluid chunk of deep house headiness, while 'Tool 6' sits somewhere between dubby tech-house and more rolling, early morning deep house.

item.title: Morgan Geist - Premise Ep
item.description: Label: Environ | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: Deep Techno
item.content:encoded:
Label: Environ

Prix: 22,00 €

Style: Deep Techno

To mark the passing of three decades since he established the now iconic Environ imprint, Morgan Geist has decided to reissue the label's long-deleted debut 12" - a solo EP that was just his second release. At the time, Geist had yet to develop the disco-leaning but naturally synth-heavy trademark sound he's become renowned for. Instead, he was investigating the stargazing potential of Detroit-influenced techno and jacking-but-spacey house. Check first the lightly bleep techno influenced excellence of 'Sands' and the more driving, upbeat and jacking 'Airpour', before diving deeply into the percussively rich deep techno wonder of 'Smear'. To complete the package, we get a suitably cosmic, pitched down ambient techno revision of the same track by The Connection Machine - back then a duo who had just released a fine EP on Planet E.

Tracklist:

  • A2. Airpour

item.title: NY STOMP - Never Forget House
item.description: Label: Clone Royal Oak | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Clone Royal Oak

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

After a period of silence, NY Stomp returns with a direct tribute to classic New York house vibes on Clone Royal Oak. The EP leans into raw drum programming, weighty basslines and sharp vocal hooks that recall the spirit of legendary Big Apple dancefloors such as The Tunnel, Twilo and Sound Factory. 'Luv Me (I Need Ur Luv)' and 'Thinkin Bout You' drive with punchy, peak-time intent, while 'Never Forget House' lands as the EP's central statement, a stripped, jacking groove built for serious systems. An instrumental version rounds things off, keeping the focus firmly on the rhythm.

item.title: Ronin - Luxury Ep
item.description: Label: Vibestate | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Vibestate

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

A quietly commanding EP from the turn of the millennium gets reissued here by Ronin on Vibestate, with all four tracks exemplifying deep, soulful house at its finest. This Ep will often fetch three figures on second-hand markets and is one of many classics for the fawned-over Driftwood label. 'Luxury' and 'Milestones' glide with signature understated elegance, while 'Coming Over To You' balances intimacy and groove with effortless poise. Closer 'Deepness Is Served' lives up to its name, a masterclass in layered textures, rich basslines and warm melodic accents. At once sexy, considered and timeless.

item.title: Kiko - World Cup (Reissue)
item.description: Label: Skylax classic | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: Techno; House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Skylax classic

Prix: 14,00 €

Style: Techno; House

There are records that do not so much belong to an era as they pass through it, leaving traces rather than statements, circulating in the margins where function outweighs discourse. World Cup, written at the end of the 1990s by Kiko, emerged in precisely that way — as a techno track whose presence was felt less through promotion than through repetition, carried from booth to booth, absorbed into the working vocabulary of DJs who recognized in it something immediate and self-evident. Its architecture is minimal yet insistent, driven by tension and release, a form of clarity that resists ornament and instead privileges duration, pressure, and movement.

item.description: Label: Clone Classic Cuts | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: Chicago House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Clone Classic Cuts

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: Chicago House

Chicago's Mike Dunn is a badass house motherfucker, as he has often declared himself on record. Here, his archive is raided by the good folk at Clone, who reissue three of Dunn's acid house tracks from 1988 and prove again why their Classic Cuts series matters. 'So Let It Be House', 'Grooving' and 'Life Goes On' have been out of print since their original release on Westbrook Records - nearly two decades of near-total obscurity for three tracks that deserve to be heard and put many new school sound-alikes to shame. They're rugged, analogue and perfectly carry the acid-soaked Chicago DNA that defined the era.

item.title: Jeff Mills - The Director's Cut Chapter 4
item.description: Label: Axis | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: Techno
item.content:encoded:
Label: Axis

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: Techno

For those new to Jeff Mills' vast - and largely incredible - back catalogue, the Director's Cut series should be essential. Like its predecessors, this fourth volume gathers together various versions of killer cuts previously produced and released by the Motor City legend over the past two decades. Highlights include deep space techno workout "Deadly Rays (Of A Hot White Sun)", the densely layered African percussion, low slung bass and echoing organ stabs of "Gateway Of Zen (Percussion Mix)", the bleep-heavy electro/techno fusion of sweaty workout "999" and the alien-sounding, minor-key hypnotism of "The Industry Of Dreams". Each track is accompanied by a separate "audio commentary" from the man himself, which is ideal for those who love to hear artists talking about their work.

item.description: Label: Endell Street | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: UK Tech House Reissue
item.content:encoded:
Label: Endell Street

Prix: 20,00 €

Endell Street returns with another essential deep-dive into London's early 2000s tech house archives. The A-side unearths the long-lost TV Babies project and their 'Deeper Situation', a hidden treasure from some of the scene's most respected selectors, complete with gritty drums and a sense of swagger that is textbook for the era. On the flip, cult duo Peace Division's heavyweight remix of Smart Alex is more leggy and funky, with loopy kicks topped with wet cymbals, an eerie breakdown and a killer drop that is punchy and authentic, so it is likely to be huge all over again two decades on.

Philly supergroup MFSB (an acronym for Mother, Father, Sister, Brother,) ended their spectacular discography with this, Mysteries of the World, a magnificent final studio album, co-written and produced with the legendary Dexter Wansel. The title track is of course the well-known, much loved and sparkling jewel in the album's crown but the whole thing is a wonderful affair with Philly soul and orchestral jazz-funk meeting in perfect harmony. The stylish and sophisticated sounds here still sound out of this world and cannot fail to get any dancefloor going.

item.title: Jeff Mills - The Director's Cut Chapter 1
item.description: Label: Axis | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: Detroit Techno
item.content:encoded:
Label: Axis

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: Detroit Techno

The Wizard is getting a little reflective in his old age. While still remaining one of the Motor City's premier futurists, Mills has decided to inaugurate a series built around overlooked or hard-to-find gems from his vast back catalogue. He begins volume one by offering up a stomping and mind-altering "Unreleased Version" of 1993 horror-techno cut "Suspense", before allowing us a second chance to enjoy the off-kilter rhythms, dystopian electronics and melancholic organ chords of 1995 classic "Gamma Player". Over on side B, you'll find the metallic, industrial style percussion, deep space riffs and thrusting drums of "Transformation B (Rotwang's Revenge)" and what appears to be an alternative version of "Exhibitionist 2" track "Hydra & Synergy". The latter is arguably the most "sci-fi techno" cut on the EP.

item.title: The Mountain People - Memorandum
item.description: Label: Mountain People | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: Tech House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Mountain People

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: Tech House

This low-key repress offers a clean update of a record long out of circulation, with three deep cuts newly edited and remastered for 45 RPM. 'Memorandum', previously heard at Giegling events, opens with slow-moving pads and a narrow rhythmic range, relying on subtle modulation rather than arrangement shifts. 'Semper' continues with more drive i a stripped-back exercise in low-end pulse and restraint, built around clipped percussion and minimal harmonic information. The B-side features the edit of 'Mountain021.1', a long-circulating favourite that trades in delay-heavy loops and soft saturation, keeping the groove linear and open-ended. The new master preserves the original's softness without dulling its detail. It's not flashy, but it's durable i functional material that wears its age lightly.

Tracklist:

  • A1. Memorandum
  • A2. Semper
  • B1. Mountain021.1 (edit & Remaster)

Opener 'Your Touch' is one of his best ever to be honest - an effortlessly smooth cut with frayed edges, humid chords running through the middle and a simple but effective vocal sample full of soul. 'June' has more bounce and a hint of New York swing from the 90s while 'Your Touch' (Tuccillo dub mix) is a playful one for the early evening. The same Ibiza based producer offers a vocal mix of Them Blues that is great for sunny outdoor sessions.

item.title: Delano Smith - Feat Diamondancer - A Message For The DJ ( Jimpster Rmx)
item.description: Prix: 25,00 € | Style: Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Prix: 25,00 €

Style: Deep House

Delano Smith's "A Message For The DJ" was first released in a distant 2005 haze, but the EP has remained a classic ever since. That's because it's a prime example of the combined powers of old-school Detroit techno and more contemporary waves of European deep house; Smith is a master of this artform, and this particular release, out on Detroit's own Still Music, has the ability to please all sorts of listeners and club-dwellers. The lead tune is full-bodied groove, taking inspiration from the US' heritage, but taking the percussion that one bit closer to what many would term 'minimal'. "Inception Dub" is just as classy and laid-back, a dreamy house assemblage with seductive jazzy nuances, leaving main man Jimpster to remix "A Message For The DJ" into a more driving, more charging tech-house monster that is perhaps the pinnacle of the entire subgenre. A piece of contemporary dance music history, right here...

Tracklist:

  • A1. A Message For The DJ
  • A2. Inception Dub
  • B1. A Message For The DJ (Jimpster Red Light remix)

item.content:encoded:

Style: Deep House

Rush Hour did us plenty of favours this year but by far our most cherished was the reissue of James Mason's timeless, proto-house excursions on the infamous "Nightgruv" EP. There's really not much to be said about these peerless productions, the original mix is a stunning voyage through glimmering synths backed by a chugging beat groove, but the unreleased longer edit is the one - voyaging through those gorgeous drums and piano keys like there's no tomorrow! "I Want Your Love" is another masterpiece - slo-mo hip-hop beats mixed in with those killer funk bass lines and the infamous vocals taking you to another dimension.

Tracklist:
